tips.comment: Willie Mullins' bumper runners were in good form at Galway last week, and debutant Boo Radley looks the one to be with here. He is related to two winners, and with Patrick Mullins riding, he looks the most likely winner here.

the model I run suggests Ripsnorter can win this one. Ripsnorter lines up here with the highest RPR of this larger 16 runner field but carries the same weight as all the other runners. Jockey on board claims a further 5 lbs which helps over the 1m 7f distance. Third when last out over the same distance and looks for some improvement to go first this time. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Not much form to go on here, but I like the breeding of this horse. He is well related to some nice individuals. The trainer does well in these events.

It could be worth a small interest in Mr Master Mac. He is a big price for this bumper, but he is by one of the sires of the moment in Blue Bresil and out of an Oscar mare. He is related to a number of winners including the Grade 2 winning mare Marias Benefit. The jockey booking of John Gleeson, who is one of the best bumper jockeys, is also a positive.
Yet to win from 3 starts over hurdles but has placed in all 3 and was a good 2nd last time. Has every chance of going 1 better

Power Of Words has shown a marked improvement of late that has seen each of the last 3 outings end in a runner-up finish. That is the type of consistency which, at this level, is going to be rewarded with a win sooner rather than later.

The model I run suggests Jetaway Nana can win this one. Jetaway Nana lines up here with the third highest RPR of the larger 16-runner field but looks well treated in the weights. Steps out carrying 7 lbs less than most of the other runners and has shown some decent form coming into this. Form figures of 632 with that second place finish only being 18 days ago shows consistent improvement. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Has some decent bits of form and looks likely to be in the shake-up. Looked unlucky on his second run over hurdles back in March, a likely winner had he not made a horlicks of the last. Ran a decent race after 10 weeks off last time and looks a likely winner here.

Makes hurdling debut after running disappointingly in a bumper when last seen in October, having shaped up well on bumper debut the time before. Has a decent breeding and should make an impact over hurdles.
Flat winner who is yet to win from 4 starts over hurdles but did finish 2nd at Sligo in May last year. A repeat of that form gives every chance in this.
Bumper efforts have been decent and one of only a few here with real potential. Value option against favorite who hasn't been in great form of late.

The model I run suggests a big upset from Bella Colombia. This result has been driven by Bella Colombia having the second highest RPr for the 15 runner field but looks relatively well treated in the weights. Bella Colombia steps out carrying 10 lbs less than the top weight. Not much experience in this maiden hurdle at all, and Bella Colombia has some real improvement to make if going close. The model has issued a 'low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.75pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

The model I run suggests We're Back Again can win this one. We're Back Again lines up here with the highest RPR of the 16-runner field but has been relatively well treated in the weights. Top weight carries 11 lbs more, and others around carry a similar weight. Second when last out 29 days ago, and if improvement can be found, it should be enough to win this one. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Speculative shout here, but Camlin Park may be able to outrun current odds. The yard is in good order, picking up 2 wins during the Galway Festival, and this is their only runner today. Did manage to win a P2P, and this doesn't look like the strongest maiden hurdle.

Although Adaliz is a five-year-old mare, she has only been to the racecourse seven times, all in 2025. Her last three runs have seen her win twice and finish in the frame. Another rise in the weights to contend with, but with her trainer winning this race a couple of seasons ago, she has a chance to register another win.

The model I run suggests Rebellious Gale can win this one. Rebellious Gale has the highest RPR of the 16-runner field but an official ranking which is third from bottom. This subsequently means Rebellious Gale lines up carrying 9-12 lbs less than most of the other rivals, and that can make a difference over the longer 3m round trip. Showed good form coming second when last out only 23 days ago and looks to build on that to come in over the line first here. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator due to the small gap back to second in the race simulation. This translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
Should be fully fit having had a couple of runs. He was outpaced on the run in last time, so this step up to 3m looks sure to suit and must have a chance from this mark. Strong each-way bet.

Ballyglass Beauty looks interesting here following her improved run at Sligo last month on her second start after a long absence. She had 3 career wins, the last coming off a mark of 103 at Listowel in September '23 before injury restricted her to just one run in 2024. She did not return to the track until June when well beaten at Punchestown. 4th at Sligo, beaten just 5 lengths, was much more promising. Off a 1lb lower mark, she looks like a good EW bet with 5 places on offer.

Course and distance winner ITS NOT OVER YET should improve for the step back up in trip. We can ignore her two previous runs over inadequate trips. They should have sharpened her up for a tilt at this. She won on good and soft, so probably ground dependent. While she might be a shade high in the weights, I do think she’s probably overpriced and might hit the board, but it’s risky. Jockey Philip Enright had a double yesterday.
Hurdles winner who finished 2nd at Naas in March over fences. Not as good in 2 races since, but with ground softening, has every chance of getting home in front.
Been in good form over hurdles, winning at Cartmel last time out. Can follow up that success here and make his chasing debut a winning one.
Maidenstreetprince is still a maiden over fences after eleven attempts but he has run well in handicaps and has been placed four times. He has won over hurdles so has the pace to win over two miles.
Bumped into one last time, beaten by a gambled-on McManus runner. That looks like decent form. Reverts back to beginners chase having run in a handicap last time.

the model I run suggests an upset from Eve's Hope. This result has been driven by Eve's hope having a comparably high RPR to the other runners but looks relatively well treated in the weights. Eve's Hope carries 7 lbs less than most of the other runners in this smaller 7 horse field over the 2m round trip. The model has issued a 'moderate' stake indicator which translates to a 1pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Well up to winning one of these. Has come 2nd the last twice, with the form of his last run looking strong, with 3rd home winning next time. Running off 94 here, though nudged up a pound, is still well in on his hurdles form.

Meehall won twice last year from 6 runs. He has had three runs so far this season, running reasonably well in two of them. He was a creditable third last time at Killarney. If running to the same level again here tonight at Roscommon, he could certainly be good enough to be involved in the finish again.

No doubting he was an unlucky loser last time. Took a narrow lead at last, going better than the subsequent winner, when the saddle slipped on landing and the rider lost his irons. Had to ride the finish with little control over his mount. Worth an each-way bet here, nudged up a couple of pounds.

Cullenwaine won over this distance at Thurles last December when his handicap mark reached a minimum of 76. His form has dipped since then and his mark is back down to 78. He was 7th behind Il Silenzio who finished 3rd over course and distance in May but that horse disappointed next time at Tipperary when made favourite and pulled up. Cullenwaine could bounce back to form at 28-1.

A very open-looking staying handicap chase where Nazine looks like a likely one who will see out the trip better than most. At 18/1, it looks like great value. A couple of recent runs off today's mark, where he has been staying on late, bodes well. Especially as there will be more emphasis on stamina today with the underfoot conditions.
Was a winner at Down Royal in April but was not as good in 2 races since. On a tough mark but holds an each-way chance if finding best form.

I think the comments in a certain Racing newspaper are a little unfair regarding Charles Coakley's 11 year old Gelding DEFINITEADARE's run 32 days ago at Wexford this old boy was returning off a 234 day break in a race that looked too sharp. This Son of COURT CAVE's better Form over the tall timber has come from 23f onwards & has ran with merit the two times he's been asked to run this far with all that better form coming off marks from 80-87 (now 84). Trainer has a 60% place strike rate the past month aswell as a 60% piece strike rate when teaming up with jockey Paddy O'Hanlon the past year who has a 37.50% place strike rate here at Roscommon the past year. Any potential rain wouldnt bother this Ground versatile veteran & with odds on 33/1 currently on offer I'm happy to nail my (each way) colours to the mast with this charge.

Ocodango Boy is only first reserve, but if he gets a run, he looks interesting here. He is still a maiden after 19 starts and has never finished better than 4th, although he has filled that position four times. His best run was here on September 24 when, over a slightly longer trip, he was beaten just 7 lengths. He is now 5 lbs lower on a career-low mark and must have a good chance of running into a place, with 5 on offer, at a decent price.
Ran a shocker last time after making an encouraging reappearance the time before. Drops a pound and tries an intermediary trip. Worth an each-way bet, though tentative after the last run.
Gaelic Des Chastys has finished in 2nd place in his last three handicap chases which included this race last year. He has since run in two handicap hurdles for which his handicap mark is lower.

Was sent off at odds of 50/1 for her chasing debut at Tipperary over 20f, and although beaten a fair way, showed promise. Was stepped up to three miles for her second attempt at Downpatrick but ran a shocker for no apparent reason. As a winning pointer, she is likely to do better at some stage and can hopefully bounce back over a slightly shorter trip and back in handicap company.

The model I run suggests an upset from Greenway Machine. This result has been driven by Greenway Machine having the second highest RPR of the larger 16 runner field but an official ranking which has him third last in this larger 16 runner field. This subsequently means Greenway Machine lines up here with the third lowest weight to carry around this 2m5f round trip. The jockey on board relieves a further 5 lbs, which helps over the distance. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

The quest for bigger priced runners is often detrimental as I know I should probably leave this alone but the itch hasn't subsided since last night when I first looked at James Barcoe's 9 year old Mare HOB'S ANGEL who I've convinced myself could improve from her debut over the tall timber at Kilbeggan 11 days ago. Finding this Daughter of MAHLER's best trip has seemed a bit of a puzzle thus far but this Mare ran two 3rd places earlier this year over 19-21f over hurdles off marks of 76-77. The booking of Jockey Peter Smithers is a positive who is very good value for his 7lb claim (in my opinion) with a 31.45% place strike rate this past year. Trainer James Barcoe echoes similar figures with a 31.25% place strike rate (past month). At current odds of 33/1 with 5 places on offer, now 7lbs lighter I've convinced myself hitting the Frame on her second attempt over fences isn't a forlorn hope. It's a potential landmine for sure but I'm happy enough for very small each way stakes.
